code:
# docker-compose.yml
services:
  gateway:
    image: ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:main-latest
    ports:
      - "4000:4000"
    volumes:
      - ./litellm_config.yaml:/app/config.yaml:ro
    extra_hosts:
      - "host.docker.internal:host-gateway"
    restart: unless-stopped

  webui:
    image: ghcr.io/open-webui/open-webui:main
    ports:
      - "3000:8080"
    volumes:
      - ./webui-data:/app/backend/data
    extra_hosts:
      - "host.docker.internal:host-gateway"
    depends_on:
      - gateway
description: One YAML file that declares a two-service stack: the LiteLLM gateway and Open WebUI.

steps.description: The comment names the file `docker-compose.yml`, and the `services:` key begins the list of services. The page says Compose declares the whole stack in one YAML file.

The first service is `gateway`, running the LiteLLM image. It publishes port 4000, mounts the config file read-only with `:ro`, adds the `host.docker.internal` host entry, and restarts unless stopped.
The second service is `webui`, running the Open WebUI image. It publishes host port 3000 to container port 8080 and bind-mounts `./webui-data` into the app's data directory, so chats persist.

The `webui` service gets the same `extra_hosts` entry and a `depends_on` on `gateway`, so it waits for the gateway. The page says services reach each other by name, because Compose puts them on a private network together.

title: A Docker Compose Stack
